reason: T0042 delivered the decisive technical breakthrough for §V.F: the chess-backend modulo-scheduler blocker that defeated T0041 v1.1 kernel_av is DEFINITIVELY RESOLVED. The aie::mac<acc32, v16int8, v16int16> rewrite produces a schedule the backend accepts (0 errors, 0 critical warnings, 2 kernel tiles + 3 helpers), x86sim regression remains bit-exact (max_abs_diff=0 vs T0022 PL golden), and the analytic latency tightens from T0040's wide 65-2100 µs into a schedule-grounded 52-210 µs range with central estimate 160 µs at 1.25 GHz AIE clock (confirmed from graph.xpe). At ALL three points in the range, AIE decisively beats the PL baseline of 674 µs (3.2× at worst case II=4, 12.9× at best case II=1, 4.2× at central II=3). The remaining gap (full cycle-accurate aiesim) is a Vitis 2024.1 standalone-aiesim+GMIO+HW-target tooling limitation — kernels stall on empty streams because user main.cpp isn't executed; only full hw_emu (XSA + sw_app + qemu) would close it, which is 4-8h Vitis work beyond T0042 scope and explicitly camera-ready territory.

decision.headline_for_paper_V_F: AIE arm 160 µs analytic (52-210 µs range, II=1 to II=4 modulo schedule) vs PL 674 µs measured = 4.2× central speedup. This is a SCHEDULE-DERIVED analytic, not a best/worst-case envelope: the central II=3 estimate is what chess-backend's accepted modulo schedule actually produces.
